v74l.rule: The questions this statement is filed under, decided after you have decided it is evidence: the id of the narrowest open question in [Open questions] whose answer this statement makes more or less likely. A statement bears on a question in these ways: (1) as the question's own figure, step or estimate, or the same quantity for another period or population when no open question covers that one (a lender's guided loan growth, for its loan-growth question; an analyst's estimate of a retailer's same-store sales, for that question; a calendar-year estimate, for the fiscal-year question of the same quantity); (2) as a part or input of the question's figure: a segment's sales for the total, a product's price or volume for its revenue, an input's cost for a margin, profit for earnings per share (a carmaker's unit deliveries, for its car revenue; a jet-fuel price, for an airline's margin; a drug's price cut, for that drug's sales); (3) from the other side of the same purchases or the demand behind them: what suppliers sell to the buyers the question counts, what those buyers order or book, and the demand that drives the buyers' spending (a drug wholesaler's sales to pharmacies, for a pharmacy purchases question; an airline's growing forward bookings, for its aircraft spending; a builder's order book, for its customers' construction spending); (4) as a variant, stopgap, key part or schedule change of a product or project, for that product's or project's event question (a regulator's request for more trial data, for a drug's approval date; a failed test flight, for an aircraft's certification date; a permit delay, for a plant's start-up date); (5) as a customer's, supplier's, competitor's or market's figure, forecast or action that changes the demand, supply, competition or pricing behind the answer (a rival bank's deposit-rate cut, for a deposit-growth question; a survey of buyers' budgets, for a spending question; a supplier's capacity cut, for a margin question). Compare the specific questions before a company-wide revenue or margin question and take that one only, never a broader question beside it. When it bears on two specific questions, take the one whose quantity it measures most directly (a hotel chain's room rate, under its room-revenue question rather than travellers' spending question; a parts maker's sales to carmakers, under the carmakers' parts-spending question rather than a rival parts maker's share question). A statement that gives a separate figure for each of two questions (a drug maker's sales of two drugs in one sentence) is written as two evidence items, one under each. A shared company, industry, event or ecosystem is not a connection, and the statement need not repeat the question's words (a variant, sibling or other name of the subject counts); whoever says it, and even when it gives no period, basis or exact amount, because the weight is judged later. Plus the ids of this answer's candidates the statement supports; empty when no question and no candidate is connected, however important it sounds.
